summary: workbench/relevance.py: rank(kernel, focus_id, candidates, task=None) as the coordinator specified (size 1..4, exact int/Fraction score, reasons in words, pinned, turned_down, group; plus place, held, kind, title and separate {truth, confidence, authority}); why(), pin/turn_down/clear (through Kernel.dispatch, on the trail), marks(), note_request()/last_request(), resolve_task(), more_words(). Reasons are kept apart with whole-number weights; sizes from thresholds 60/40/20/1 with caps per size; hysteresis keeps a tile's placing score while its score stays within a tenth of it. Kernel operations relevance.why (read, observer), relevance.pin, .turn_down, .clear (execute) registered in their own 1.0 L3 blocks; registry record regenerated. Smoke on Rail Demo: 36 of 36 checks passed, the four acceptance examples among them.

decisions: Weights (whole numbers, WEIGHTS): recorded relation input 40, output 35, quoted_by 35, quotes 30, finding_on 30, question_on 30, revision_of 25, cross_ref 20, other recorded 20; inferred 6 ("possible ...; not verified"); current revision +15, archived -5 (+15 "an earlier revision, and your task looks back" when the task says history/earlier/previous/...); contradiction (refuted, held, does not hold, failed) +25; open question / open finding +25; a change affects it (recheck, stale) +20; each distinguishing task word +20 (two at most); used by the assignment's steps +40; pin +100, turn down -100. The plan leaves the weighting to the implementation (paper section 5).

Sizes: 4 from 60, 3 from 40, 2 from 20, 1 from 1; at most 4/6/8/6 tiles per size (the rest step down); a score of 0 or less, a turned-down neighbour and the overflow of size 1 form the group (group=True, "and N more" via more_words()). Pinned: size 4, first. Size 1 is a small tile, not the group, so the archived Rev A stays a tile smaller than Rev B.

Hysteresis: a neighbour keeps its placing score (size and place) while its new score is within a tenth of it (at least 2); memory per (workspace, focus, task key); a task not seen yet on that board starts from the board's latest ranking, so a new request moves only the tiles whose scores it really changes.

Task words: the task's words (her dictionary's stems, reading.stem/STOP) that occur in at least one neighbour and in no more than about half (a word on every tile, like "Rail Demo", tells nothing); a basis line's own words and plan verbs (read, write, check ...) are not counted.

"The owner's last request" had no record in the tree, so relevance keeps one (table relevance_request, one row per owner, replaced each time, the task for 12 hours); SlateFace.ask in shell2.py notes it (guarded, 1.0 L3). It is a direct write of the owner's own words, not a Kernel operation (no new op beyond the four asked for).

The active assignment is the newest open K1 assignment not stopped (assignments.active_work + status): its objective and step titles are the task's words, the record ids in its steps' inputs and outputs are what it "uses".

rank() takes no principal: it reads as the desk owner (engineering_kernel.operator()). A candidate without a title gets one through observer reads (office.get, documents.get, intake.item, investigation.path, objects.get), cached 30 s, and only when there is a task to match.

The owner's marks are per board (focus), in table relevance_marks; pin/turn_down/clear go through Kernel.dispatch as the owner, so they are audited and on the activity trail; relevance.why is an observer (asking is not an event).
findings_for_the_coordinator: L2: candidates may carry an optional "title" (else relevance reads it through the Kernel when a task is set), "stale" (a change affects it) and "words"; rank() rows also carry place, held, kind, title and separate {truth, confidence, authority} for the tile's own marks. relation is read as "candidate <relation> focus" (input = supplies the focus; quoted_by = quoted in the focus). more_words(rows) gives "and 12 more".
relevance.why answers from the window process's memory of the latest ranking; from another process (CLI) it says "not on this board now" with the owner's mark.
P1 (her column) may want to call relevance.note_request from its own "ask Kasandra..." line if it does not go through SlateFace.ask.
